rounds.proof_sketch: total_elements=67,108,864, block_size=256. Original formula gives 262,144 blocks; mutated gives 262,145 blocks. Extra block has thread indices [67,108,864..67,109,119], all >= total_elements, so all threads return immediately due to 'if (idx >= total_elements) return;' guard.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the grid launch calculation from (n+255)/256 to (n+257)/256, resulting in one extra CUDA block being launched for this specific input size. However, the kernel has an explicit bounds check that causes all threads with idx >= total_elements to return immediately without any memory operations. Since the output tensor is correctly sized and all valid indices are still processed by the original block count, the extra block contributes nothing and produces no observable difference. Furthermore, the mutation is only in the inference code path, which requires the model to be in eval mode.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation only affects grid launch count in inference mode, and the extra block's threads all exit immediately due to bounds checking. No value pattern can cause divergence.
rounds.recommendations: When testing CUDA grid launch mutations, ensure tests cover both training and inference code paths (model.train() and model.eval()). Also consider that mutations affecting only grid size may be equivalent when bounds checks prevent out-of-range threads from executing.
